4a1931fa10b922ad15bb3b731a6dc803148426c8\nAuthor: Ewrdad Server <[REDACTED EMAIL]>\nDate:   Sat Oct 31 00:05:25 2026 +0000\n\n    Harden runner log transport and live fan-out (stage cleanup)\n    \n    Surfacing agent logs to the UI regressed in edge cases after the\n    monolith→runner switch; this tightens the structured log pipeline so it\n    fails safe and loses nothing observable:\n    \n    - runner/logEvents.js: flush()/close() now DRAIN — events queued while a\n      batch is in flight ship before close() resolves, so the trailing batch\n      always lands before the stage completion report (previously close()\n      could return with events still pending). The text fallback now converts\n      everything not yet sent (failed batch AND pending queue), not just the\n      failed batch, so nothing vanishes mid-transition.\n    - runner/daemon.js: flush the structured sender on the generic interrupt\n      path too, so the tool/error trail up to a mid-run failure is stored.\n    - api/flow/executionLedger.js: ingestLogEvents validates and JSON-clones\n      events BEFORE any task mutation — an invalid batch with a seq gap is\n      rejected 400 without writing a spurious \"frames missing\" marker, and\n      the seq cursor stays put so a corrected retry is not a gap.\n    - api/flow/runnerRoutes.js: the live PROCESS_STDOUT fan-out from\n      POST /tasks/:id/logs is redacted at broadcast (older Runners ship raw\n      text on the fallback path; storage was already redacted, the socket\n      was not).\n    - frontend logEntryModel.js: stored/live dedupe keys are lane-namespaced\n      (text vs structured) — the two lanes keep independent seq counters on\n      the same execution, so a bare executionId:seq key could hide a live\n      frame during the fallback transition.\n    - frontend logs/adapters.js: PROCESS_LOG_ENTRIES live items render the\n      carried record's real text/kind/payload (tool cards, timings, thinking\n      markers) in monitor surfaces like the Live Console instead of blank\n      rows.\n    - api/redactSecrets.test.js renamed to redactSecrets.shared.test.js to\n      match the shared-module test convention (toolLogFormat.shared.test.js).\n    - site-docs/unified-logging.md: document the broadcast-point redaction.\n    \n    Tests: drain-on-close and fallback-converts-pending (runner), invalid\n    batch with seq gap writes no marker (ledger), WS fan-out redaction for\n    both lanes over HTTP (routes), lane-namespaced dedupe and structured\n    live-entry adaptation (frontend).  Harden runner log transport and live fan-out (stage cleanup)\n    \n    Surfacing agent logs to the UI regressed in edge cases after the\n    monolith→runner switch; this tightens the structured log Null when absent or\n *   unparseable — callers treat that as permissive, never a block.\n * @example coerceRunnerVersion('v1.2.3') => '1.2.3'\n ***/\nexport const coerceRunnerVersion = (version) => {\n\tif (typeof version !== \"string\") return null;\n\tconst cleaned = version.trim().replace(/^v/, \"\");\n\tif (!cleaned) return null;\n\ttry {\n\t\tconst coerced = semver.coerce(cleaned);\n\t\treturn coerced ? coerced.version : null;\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn null;\n\t}\n};\n\n/***\n * MARK: runnerVersionAtLeast\n * @description Whether a reported Runner product version meets a floor.\n *   Permissive (true) when either side is missing or malformed, so\n *   introducing a floor can never lock the fleet out.\n * @example runnerVersionAtLeast('0.2.0', '0.1.0') => true\n ***/\nexport const runnerVersionAtLeast = (runnerVersion, minVersion) => {\n\tconst have = coerceRunnerVersion(runnerVersion);\n\tconst floor = coerceRunnerVersion(minVersion);\n\tif (!have) return true;\n\tif (!floor) return true;\n\ttry {\n\t\treturn semver.gte(have, floor);\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn true;\n\t}\n};\n\n/***\n * MARK: belowMinimumRunnerVersion\n * @description Whether a KNOWN Runner version sits below the dispatch\n *   floor (the 409 condition). The new backend has both endpoints, so it would accept text logs via `/tasks/:id/logs`. ✓\\n3. **New runner → Old backend**: The new runner tries to send structured events to `/tasks/:id/log-events`, gets a 404, falls back to text logs via `/tasks/:id/logs`. ✓\\n\\nSo the changes are **backward compatible**! Existing installations won't break on update.\\n\\nNow let me write a summary and provide the verdict.\"},{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"Based on my analysis of the logging infrastructure changes, I can now determine whether the current implementation would break existing installations on update.\\n\\n## Analysis Summary\\n\\nThe logging changes were implemented in commit `4a1931f` which hardened the runner log transport pipeline. back to text logs\\n2. **api/flow/executionLedger.js**: Added validation for structured log events\\n3. **api/flow/runnerRoutes.js**: Added log-events endpoint and text frame redaction\\n4. **frontend/src/components/tasks/logEntryModel.js**: Added lane-namespaced dedupe keys\\n\\n### Backward Compatibility Analysis:\\n\\n**Scenario 1: Old Runner (pre-structured logs) → New Backend**\\n- Old runner only has `client.logs()` method (text-based endpoint `/tasks/:id/logs`)\\n- New backend has BOTH `/tasks/:id/logs` (text) and `/tasks/:id/log-events` (structured)\\n- Old runner sends text logs to `/tasks/:id/logs` → **WORKS ✓**\\n\\n**Scenario 2: New Runner → Old Backend**\\n- New runner has both `client.logs()` and `client.logEvents()` methods\\n- New runner first tries `/tasks/:id/log-events` (structured)\\n- Old backend doesn't have this endpoint → returns 404\\n- Runner detects version skew (404/405) → sets `structured = false`\\n- Runner falls back to text logs via `/tasks/:id/logs` → **WORKS ✓**\\n\\n**Scenario 3: New Runner → New Backend**\\n- Both endpoints available, structured logs work perfectly → **WORKS ✓**\\n\\n### Version Compatibility:\\n- Runner API version: 1.0.0 (requires backend >=1.0.0 <2.0.0)\\n- Backend API version: 1.0.0\\n- Version compatibility check exists for critical endpoints but NOT for log-events (intentional for backward So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible\n6|\n7|### Principles\n8|\n9|- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive\n10|- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”\n11|- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)\n12|- File structure should reflect the call stack\n13|- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english\n14|- Include why things are done not just what is done\n15|- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)\n16|- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS\n17|- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality\n18|  \n19|  \n20|\n21|## Functional over Object oreintated\n22|\n23|Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).\n24|\n25|### Principles\n26|\n27|- Try and avoid using classes where possible\n28|- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that\n29|- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects\n30|- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.\n31|- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something\n32|- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.\n33|- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility\n34|\n35|\n36|## Co-location over abstraction\n37|\n38|Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.\n39|\n40|### Principles\n41|- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file\n42|- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`\n43|- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.\n44|- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders\n45|- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.\n46|- Don’t fear repetition of code\n47|- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.\n48|- Use folders as a tool for organising\n49|\n50|## Tested over trusted \n51|\n52|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. \n53|\n54|### Principles\n55|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function\n56|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe\n57|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately\n58|- Tests must be consistent\n59|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app\n60|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle\n61|\n62|\n63|## Fast iteration over long planning\n64|\n65|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.\n66|\n67|### Principles\n68|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed\n69|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.\n70|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.\n71|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon\n72|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small\n73|- Make change easy, then make the change. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.\n48|- Use folders as a tool for organising\n49|\n50|## Tested over trusted \n51|\n52|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. \n53|\n54|### Principles\n55|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function\n56|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe\n57|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately\n58|- Tests must be consistent\n59|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app\n60|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle\n61|\n62|\n63|## Fast iteration over long planning\n64|\n65|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.\n66|\n67|### Principles\n68|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed\n69|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.\n70|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.\n71|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon\n72|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small\n73|- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.\n74|\n75|\n76|\n77|# Inspirations\n78|My principles here are inspired by:\n79|\n80|- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)\n81|- Life isn’t binary (book)\n82|- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)\n83|\n84|\n85|# Examples\n86|\n87|## Intent Driven descriptions\n88|\n89|### Bad Example\n90|\n91|```js\n92|\n93|const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {\n94|\n95|    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}\n96|\n97|    users.push(user)\n98|  \n99|}\n100|\n101|const list = []\n102|\n103|userFactory(\"Frank\",32,list)\n104|\n105|\n106|```\n107|\n108|## Good example\n109|\n110|```js\n111|\n112|/**\n113|* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear\n114|* @description calculates the age someone will be next year\n115|* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  \n116|console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4\n117|*/\n118|const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {\n119|  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1\n120|  \n121|  return ageNextYear\n122|}\n123|\n124|const userObjectsList = []\n125|\n126|const usersName = \"Frank\"\n127|const usersAge = 32\n128|\n129|const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})\n130|\n131|userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})\n132|\n133|\n134|```","partials":"Read text file `docs/KB Code Standards.md`.\n1|# Values\n2|\n3|## User understandable over technical language\n4|\n5|I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible\n6|\n7|### Principles\n8|\n9|- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive\n10|- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”\n11|- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)\n12|- File structure should reflect the call stack\n13|- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english\n14|- Include why things are done not just what is done\n15|- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)\n16|- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS\n17|- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality\n18|  \n19|  \n20|\n21|## Functional over Object oreintated\n22|\n23|Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).\n24|\n25|### Principles\n26|\n27|- Try and avoid using classes where possible\n28|- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that\n29|- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects\n30|- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.\n31|- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something\n32|- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.\n33|- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility\n34|\n35|\n36|## Co-location over abstraction\n37|\n38|Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.\n39|\n40|### Principles\n41|- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file\n42|- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.\n46|- Don’t fear repetition of code\n47|- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. Grouping, filtering, search, severity,\n8| *   and detail expansion all live in the unified viewer\n9| *   (`frontend/src/components/logs/`); this module only normalizes.\n10| *\n11| *   The tag grammar is the shared `classifyLogLineTag`\n12| *   (`shared/logTagGrammar.js`) — the same module the API-side synthesis\n13| *   reads, so stored history and this parse can never disagree:\n14| *     [TOOL] [RESULT]      -> kind \"tool\"       (tools feed)\n15| *     [THINKING]           -> kind \"thinking\"   (thinking feed)\n16| *     [USAGE]              -> kind \"telemetry\"  (telemetry feed)\n17| *     [RAW]                -> kind \"raw\"        (raw feed)\n18| *     [PERM] [PLAN]        -> kind \"permission\"/\"plan\" (main feed)\n19| *     [ERROR] [FAIL]       -> kind \"error\"      (main feed)\n20| *     [AGENT]              -> kind \"assistant\"  (main feed)\n21| *     [INFO] [SYSTEM] [GIT] [CI] [CI/CMD] [HUMAN] [WARN] -> kind \"system\"\n22| *     untagged text        -> kind \"assistant\"  (main feed)\n23| */\n24|\n25|import { classifyLogLineTag } from '../../../../shared/logTagGrammar.js';\n26|\n27|/***\n28| * MARK: legacyLogEntryId\n29| * @description Stable synthetic id for a parsed legacy log line.\n30| ***/\n31|let legacyEntryCounter = 0;\n32|const legacyLogEntryId = () => {\n33|  legacyEntryCounter += 1;\n34|  return `legacy-log-${legacyEntryCounter}`;\n35|};\n36|\n37|/***\n38| * MARK: entryFromLogLine\n39| * @description Maps one rendered log line to a structured entry using the\n40| *   shared tag grammar (`classifyLogLineTag`) — the single source this\n41| *   parse and the backend synthesis both read, so a tag can never\n42| *   classify one way in stored history and another way live. Untagged\n43| *   text is assistant narrative.\n44| * @example entryFromLogLine('[TOOL] bash(\"ls\")') => { kind: 'tool', feed: 'tools', text: '…' }\n45| * @param {string} line\n46| * @returns {Object} A structured log entry.\n47| ***/\n48|export function entryFromLogLine(line) {\n49|  const { kind, feed } = classifyLogLineTag(line);\n50|  return {\n51|    id: legacyLogEntryId(),\n52|    ts: null,\n53|    feed,\n54|    feeds: [feed],\n55|    kind,\n56|    turn: null,\n57|    text: String(line),\n58|    meta: { source: 'legacy-process-logs' },\n59|  };\n60|}\n61|\n62|/***\n63| * MARK: parseLegacyProcessLogs\n64| * @description Parses the legacy `task.processLogs` text into structured\n65| *   entries: blank lines are dropped, consecutive duplicates are de-duped\n66| *   (the exact behavior of today's line-based Logs tab).\n67| * @example parseLegacyProcessLogs('[INFO] a\\n[INFO] a') => [entry('[INFO] a')]\n68| * @param {string} text\n69| * @returns {Array<Object>} Structured log entries.\n70| ***/\n71|export function parseLegacyProcessLogs(text) {\n72|  if (!text || typeof text !== 'string') return [];\n73|  const lines = text.split('\\n').filter((l) => l.trim());\n74|  const result = [];\n75|  for (const line of lines) {\n76|    if (result.length === 0 || result.at(-1).text !== line) {\n77|      result.push(entryFromLogLine(line));\n78|    }\n79|  }\n80|  return result;\n81|}\n82|\n83|/***\n84| * MARK: normalizeEntries\n85| * @description Returns the task's structured log entries when present, or\n86| *   synthesizes them from the legacy processLogs text otherwise. WebSocket\n87| *   process lines (live system output) are appended as system entries.\n88| * @example normalizeEntries(task) => [entry, …]\n89| * @param {Object} task - The task (may carry logEntries and/or processLogs).\n90| * @param {Array<Object>} [wsProcessLines] - Live process:stdout lines from the WebSocket.\n91| * @returns {Array<Object>} Structured log entries.\n92| ***/\n93|export function normalizeEntries(task, wsProcessLines = []) {\n94|  const structured = Array.isArray(task?.logEntries) ? task.logEntries.filter(Boolean) : [];\n95|  const base = structured.length > 0 ? [...structured] : parseLegacyProcessLogs(task?.processLogs);\n96|  // Frames already persisted (keyed by lane + execution + seq) must not\n97|  // reappear as live lines after a refetch: the socket pushes each frame\n98|  // the moment it is ingested, and the same frame lands in stored entries\n99|  // on the next task fetch. The lane prefix matters: the text lane\n100|  // (process:stdout) and the structured lane (PROCESS_LOG_ENTRIES) keep\n101|  // INDEPENDENT seq counters on the same execution, so a bare\n102|  // `executionId:seq` key could collide across lanes during the fallback\n103|  // transition and hide a frame that was never stored. Frames without an\n104|  // identity (legacy CI lines) always pass through, as before.\n105|  const storedKeys = new Set();\n106|  for (const entry of base) {\n107|    const meta = entry?.meta;\n108|    if (meta && meta.executionId != null && meta.seq != null) {\n109|      const lane = meta.source === 'runner-structured' ? 'structured' : 'text';\n110|      storedKeys.add(`${lane}:${meta.executionId}:${meta.seq}`);\n111|    }\n112|  }\n113|  const live = [];\n114|  for (const p of Array.isArray(wsProcessLines) ? wsProcessLines : []) {\n115|    if (!p) continue;\n116|    if (p.executionId != null && p.seq != null) {\n117|      const lane = p.entry && typeof p.entry === 'object' ? 'structured' : 'text';\n118|      if (storedKeys.has(`${lane}:${p.executionId}:${p.seq}`)) {\n119|        continue;\n120|      }\n121|    }\n122|    // Structured live entries (`PROCESS_LOG_ENTRIES` frames): the backend\n123|    // record rides along untouched — same shape as stored history, so the\n124|    // viewer renders tool cards, timings, and expandable details live.\n125|    if (p.entry && typeof p.entry === 'object') {\n126|      live.push({\n127|        ...p.entry,\n128|        meta: {\n129|          ...(p.entry.meta || {}),\n130|          source: p.entry.meta?.source || 'ws-log-entries',\n131|          ...(p.executionId != null ? { executionId: p.executionId } : {}),\n132|          ...(p.seq != null ? { seq: p.seq } : {}),\n133|          ...(p.runnerId != null ? { runnerId: p.runnerId } : {}),\n134|        },\n135|      });\n136|      continue;\n137|    }\n138|    // WS records carry a `[Project] ` prefix; strip one leading bracket\n139|    // group so the tag grammar classifies the actual line kind.\n140|    const line = p.raw || `${p.tag || '[INFO]'} ${p.text || ''}`;\n141|    const entry = entryFromLogLine(String(line).replace(/^\\[[^\\]\\n]+\\] (?=\\[)/, ''));\n142|    // The socket line already carries a stable id (minted once when the\n143|    // line arrived): reuse it so live rows keep their React keys and\n144|    // expansion state across recomputes instead of remounting on every\n145|    // new line. Lines without one keep a synthetic id, as before.\n146|    if (p.id != null) entry.id = p.id;\n147|    entry.meta = {\n148|      ...(entry.meta || {}),\n149|      source: 'ws-process-logs',\n150|      ...(p.executionId != null ? { executionId: p.executionId } : {}),\n151|      ...(p.seq != null ? { seq: p.seq } : {}),\n152|      ...(p.runnerId != null ? { runnerId: p.runnerId } : {}),\n153|    };\n154|    live.push(entry);\n155|  }\n156|  return [...base, ...live];\n157|}\n158|\n159|/***\n160| * MARK: fullTextIndex\n161| * @description Indexes entries by id so collapsed thinking markers can look\n162| *   up their full thinking block.\n163| * @example fullTextIndex(entries).get(marker.meta.fullTextId)?.text\n164| * @param {Array<Object>} entries\n165| * @returns {Map} Map of entry id -> entry.\n166| ***/\n167|export function fullTextIndex(entries) {\n168|  return new Map((entries || []).map((entry) => [entry.id, entry]));\n169|}"}},{"id":27,"ts":"2026-11-03T14:24:09.652Z","feed":"tools","feeds":["tools"],"kind":"tool","turn":1,"text":"[RESULT] Read text file `shared/logTagGrammar.js`. 1|/** 2| * MARK: logTagGrammar 3| * @description The ONE tag grammar mapping a rendered log line to its 4| * structured entry kind and feed. No two\n20| *   rules overlap, so the order is documentation, not behavior — except\n21| *   that these run against the STDOUT-unwrapped line (see\n22| *   `classifyLogLineTag`).\n23| * @example LOG_LINE_TAG_RULES[0] => { pattern: /^\\[(TOOL|RESULT)\\]/, kind: 'tool', feed: 'tools' }\n24| ***/\n25|const LOG_LINE_TAG_RULES = Object.freeze([\n26|\t{ pattern: /^\\[(TOOL|RESULT)\\]/, kind: \"tool\", feed: \"tools\" },\n27|\t// One rule covers `[RUNNER]` and `[runner <id>]`: after `[runner` the\n28|\t// next character is either `]` (caps form) or a space (inline form).\n29|\t{ pattern: /^\\[runner[\\] ]/i, kind: \"runner\", feed: \"main\" },\n30|\t{ pattern: /^\\[THINKING\\]/, kind: \"thinking\", feed: \"thinking\" },\n31|\t{ pattern: /^\\[USAGE\\]/, kind: \"telemetry\", feed: \"telemetry\" },\n32|\t{ pattern: /^\\[RAW\\]/, kind: \"raw\", feed: \"raw\" },\n33|\t{ pattern: /^\\[PERM\\]/, kind: \"permission\", feed: \"main\" },\n34|\t{ pattern: /^\\[PLAN\\]/, kind: \"plan\", feed: \"main\" },\n35|\t// Case-insensitive like every other error check in the UI: a lowercase\n36|\t// `[error]` line is still an error, not narrative.\n37|\t{ pattern: /^\\[(ERROR|FAIL|STDERR)\\]/i, kind: \"error\", feed: \"main\" },\n38|\t{\n39|\t\tpattern: /^\\[(INFO|SYSTEM|GIT|CI\\/CMD|CI|HUMAN|WARN)\\]/,\n40|\t\tkind: \"system\",\n41|\t\tfeed: \"main\",\n42|\t},\n43|\t{ pattern: /^\\[AGENT\\]/, kind: \"assistant\", feed: \"main\" },\n44|]);\n45|\n46|/***\n47| * MARK: classifyLogLineTag\n48| * @description Maps one rendered log chunk to its structured entry kind and\n49| *   feed using the shared tag grammar. strict match.\n40|      if (parsed.harness !== hid) continue;\n41|      out.push({\n42|        key: id,\n43|        id: parsed.form === 'harnessReasoning' ? `${parsed.id}::${parsed.reasoning}` : parsed.id,\n44|        provider: parsed.provider,\n45|        name: parsed.id,\n46|        fleet: true,\n47|      });\n48|    } else if (parsed.form === 'provider') {\n49|      out.push({ key: id, id: The UI should feel like watching Muse Code work\n7|live, step by step, with full detail available as searchable history. This is a\n8|log-fidelity and transport parity task, not a product change: no new AI\n9|summaries, reuse existing structured log machinery.\n10|\n11|## Success Criteria (from the survey)\n12|\n13|- Live, step-by-step viewing of an agent running (Q1).\n14|- Always visible, using only data that already exists (Q2 + note \"don't use AI to generate summaries\"):\n15|  - short status updates,\n16|  - actions taken (files read/changed, commands run),\n17|  - full command/tool results,\n18|  - errors and retries,\n19|  - per-step timings.\n20|- The same detail available live and as history (Q3), i.e. full transparency.\n21|- Long-term retention, and the log must be searchable (Q4).\n22|- Secrets and PII are removed automatically before display, persistence, and any commit (Q5), because logs may land in the repository.\n23|- Existing gates stay green: `npm run test:unit`, `npm run lint`, focused log suites and headless screenshot checks.\n24|\n25|## Survey Constraints (binding)\n26|\n27|Taken from `SURVEY.md`:\n28|\n29|- Q1: \"Like watching it work live, step by step (Muse Code style)\".\n30|- Q2: all five detail classes; \"Only use things that already exist, don't use AI to generate summaries\".\n31|- Q3: \"Both live and history\" (\"Full transparency\").\n32|- Q4: \"Keep everything and make it searchable\".\n33|- Q5: \"Yes, hide secrets automatically\" plus PII, so committed logs stay safe.\n34|\n35|## Current-State Evidence (why fidelity was lost)\n36|\n37|### A. The structured pipeline already exists in-process\n38|\n39|- Normalized agent events are defined in `api/agent/sessionEvents.js` as\n40|  `AGENT_EVENT_NAMES`:\n41|  `run_started`, `assistant_delta`, `message_started`,\n42|  `tool_started`, `tool_updated`, `tool_finished`,\n43|  `run_finished`, `run_error`,\n44|  plus unified-log events\n45|  `usage_updated`, `session_meta`, `permission_requested`,\n46|  `permission_resolved`, `plan_updated`, `reasoning_delta`,\n47|  `harness_log`.\n48|- `api/agent/logStream/logProcessor.js` turns those events into canonical,\n49|  grouped records over feeds `main`, `thinking`, `tools`, `telemetry`, `raw`.\n50|- `api/agent/logStream/agentLogStreamer.js` wraps the processor and exposes\n51|  `handleEvent`, `system`, `consumeFeed`, `snapshot`, `renderText`,\n52|  `renderFeed`; `agentRunner.js` uses it in the embedded path and passes\n53|  entries through `onChunk`.\n54|- `api/watch/processLogs.js` renders legacy tags from structured entries,\n55|  synthesizes entries for system/GIT/CI/RUNNER lines, manages entry caps\n56|  (`_appendProcessLog`, `_appendLogEntries`, `_replaceLogEntries`,\n57|  `_capLogEntries`), and maps runner frames to kind `runner`.\n58|\n59|### B. The embedded path already preserves this\n60|\n61|In `api/flow/execution/executeStage.js` (embedded mode), `agentRunner(...)`\n62|receives `onChunk`; each chunk (`entry.text`) is appended via\n63|`_appendProcessLog` while running, and after the stage\n64|`_replaceLogEntries(task, startIndex, result.logEntries)` upgrades the\n65|synthesized entries to the streamer's structured entries. The candidate\n66|UI then receives everything through `adaptTaskEntries` in\n67|`frontend/src/components/tasks/LogsPanel.jsx` -> `LogViewer`.\n68|\n69|### C. The runner boundary only carries text — this is the regression\n70|\n71|- `runner/harness.js::runHarnessStage` subscribes to the session but forwards\n72|  only:\n73|  - `assistant_delta.delta` as `event.delta`\n74|  - `harness_log.text` as `event.text`,\n75|  and only those two. It drops `tool_started/updated/finished` (args, full\n76|  results, timings), `reasoning_delta`, `usage_updated`, `permission_*`,\n77|  `plan_updated`, and structured error/retry data. It returns only `output`.\n78|- `runner/daemon.js` turns any `onLog(text)` call into newline-split chunks via\n79|  `sendLogs`, each POSTed to `/tasks/:id/logs` with `bytes` only.\n80|- `api/flow/executionLedger.js::ingestLogs` treats each frame as a text string\n81|  and calls `_appendProcessLog(task, \\`[runner ${runnerId}] ${bytes}\\`, ...)`.\n82|  That is why the UI only sees runner-prefixed text chunks instead of\n83|  `[TOOL]`/`[RESULT]`/`[THINKING]`/telemetry records with args and timings.\n84|- `api/flow/execution/applyRunnerReport.js` persists `outcome.output`\n85|  (final assistant text) into the stage report and uses it as\n86|  `streamedOutput`; it does not restore tool, thinking, usage, or timing\n87|  entries. (Exit-code/output tail behavior is retained.)\n88|- `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js::/tasks/:id/logs` additionally emits a\n89|  `process:stdout` socket event limited to the runner-prefixed text chunk,\n90|  so the live tail matches the coarse ingest.\n91|\n92|### D. UI already has the viewer we need\n93|\n94|- `frontend/src/components/logs/` contains `LogViewer.jsx`, `adapters.js`,\n95|  `logCategories.js`, `logViewerState.js` with category chips, search, density,\n96|  timestamps, grouped expandable rows, and follow-scroll. The task surface\n97|  calls `useTaskLogs` -> `adaptTaskEntries`.\n98|- `shared/toolLogFormat/` contains `summarizeToolStart`, `summarizeToolResult`,\n99|  `summarizeUsage`, `summarizePermission`, `summarizePlan`, `stripAnsi`, plus\n100|  normalization/truncation helpers. This is the canonical formatter; do not\n101|  duplicate it.\n102|- Redaction today is environment-variable-name based only:\n103|  `api/agent/harnesses/shared/harnessScaffold.js` exports\n104|  `SECRET_NAME_PATTERN`, used to drop secret-shaped env vars from child envs.\n105|  There is no content/PII redactor for log text; one must be introduced.\n106|- Caps: `config.logEntriesMaxCount` defaults to 500 (from schema/tests).\n107|  Survey Q4 (\"keep everything\") conflicts with the current eviction policy and\n108|  needs an explicit decision (pagination/archive, not silent truncation).\n109|\n110|## Principle used throughout\n111|\n112|Make change easy first (refactors, redaction choke point, structured transport\n113|plumbing with no behavior change), then make the change (widen forwarding,\n114|persist/stream everything, render everything). Research that decides the shape\n115|of the work comes before coding changes.\n116|\n117|## Phase 0 — Research first (big unknowns; no behavior change)\n118|\n119|- R1 Runner->backend log path audit (done largely above; finalize exact\n120|  client contract): confirm `runner/client.js::logs` payload constraints,\n121|  batching, retry, and whether a structured-event upload is viable or requires\n122|  a new endpoint/field. Output: event-coverage matrix with rows = 17\n123|  normalized AGENT_EVENT_NAMES and runner columns `forward`,\n124|  `preserve order`, `backend ingest`, `live socket`, `persisted`,\n125|  `UI render`; mark current-state pass/drop, and the target state every row\n126|  must reach.\n127|- R2 Backend->UI/live path audit: map `api/routes/ws.js`, `api/eventBridge.js`,\n128|  `api/routes/sessions.js`, task log endpoints, `useWebSocket`, `useTaskLogs`,\n129|  `adaptTaskEntries`, `fullTextIndex`, and `normalizeEntries`. Confirm (a)\n130|  whether WS delivers structured entries or only process lines, (b) what the\n131|  logs tab refetches after run completion, and (c) how history is retained\n132|  and capped. never silently drop events except\n195|    under the existing eviction marker.\n196|  - Push the same events to live WS channel with structured entry shape, not\n197|    only the `[runner ...]` text line; dashboard's widget catalog includes a **Harness Reliability** widget (off by\n \n While the monitor is open and a task is running, KainBain holds a Screen Wake Lock so the screen does not dim or sleep on desktop or mobile — like a video player. It is on by default and can be turned off in UI Customization › Workspace (\"Keep screen awake while monitoring\", `keepScreenAwakeOnMonitor` in `kainbain_ui_preferences`). The lock needs a supporting browser and a secure context, so on plain-`http://` LAN installs the feature silently does nothing (the settings row says so); leaving the monitor, idling, or hiding the tab releases the lock immediately.\n \n+## Agent logs\n+\n+The task Logs tab shows the same structured entries live and as history:\n+assistant narrative, thinking traces (short markers in the narrative, full\n+blocks behind the Thinking filter), tool calls with arguments, tool results\n+with per-step timings, errors and retries, permission prompts, plan updates,\n+usage telemetry, and raw wire evidence. Live entries arrive over the socket as\n+they are ingested; history is the same records re-read from the task, so a\n+reload shows exactly what streamed. Search is case-insensitive across the\n+rendered text, expandable details, tool names/arguments/results, and metadata.\n+\n+Retention is bounded: at most `KAINBAIN_LOG_ENTRIES_MAX_COUNT` entries (default\n+500) are kept per task, with telemetry (default 100) and raw-evidence (default\n+50) sub-budgets inside it.
